questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility to improve my language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy. Very limited transparency in regard to the available courses and particularly the structure of the courses meaning the litterature, focus of the clases and format of the exam.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction meetings arranged by the host-university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. Recommend to find and engage in the various Whatsapp-groups available and to seek out recommendations from previous exchange students as well as the local exchange organizations. And call the potential landlord to try and minimize the risk of being scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its cheaper and more central. However, there is and increased risk of being scammed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process in itself is relatively easy as you enter the details of the course online in order to register. However, the process of finding relevant courses is very hard as there is no guide on where to find available courses at your faculty, all courses are based on last years course-catalouge (meaning you have no guarantee that they will become available for your exchange semester), and the time-slots of the courses changes (meaning you are very likely to end up with overlapping courses forcing you to re-do the entire process of finding new courses, which dont overlap).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None, you have to find it all on your own.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to spent a lot of time on the process. This is due to the fact that it is hard to find the available courses, the information of what the courses actually contain is very limited and you have no guarantee of the availability or time-slot of the specific course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic-level is non-existing. There is no critical or original thinking, and the obligatory literature is extremely limited. There is no structure of the classes and the academic output of the classes is limited to what you could read on Wikipedia or what you learn in High School.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at UGR is dominated by teachers and students who arrive late to class (Teachers arrive up to 15 minutes late and students up to 30 minutes), students interrupt the professor with irrelevant comments or questions and most of the teaching is unstructured, meaning that a class include various subjects without explaining the connection between them or going into depth on any of the subjects. The few students who actually show up to class are unfocused and talk lively to each other during class without the professor asking for silence.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. ELECTORAL ANALYSIS
2. CONTEMPORARY POLITICAL HISTORY OF SPAIN
3. INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS
4. POLITICAL SYSTEMS OF EMERGING COUNTRIES
5. POLITICAL SYSTEMS IN THE MAGHREB

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend 1) Electoral Analysis and 2) International Organisations. Even though the academic level in both courses is low, the teachers are great to engage and communicate the material and your knowledge of each subject increases greatly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was never introduced to any activities arranged by my university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Engage in social activities outside of the exchange community such as local running or sports clubs. The communities of exchange students is primarily based on partying and drinking, so I would strongly recommend to engage in social activities with the locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Andalusia offers a lot of places to visit such as Sevilla, Cordoba, Malaga ect. Its easy and cheap to travel in Spain.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was hard to adjust to the academic culture at the university as there was no critical thinking or requirements to read relevant litterature. However, the local culture of Spain is amazing with very open people and great opportunities to eat out and explore the city as well as the rest of Andalusia and Spain.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in local clubs or communities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open culture and that everyone can talk to everyone.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) If you have any academic aspirations, don´t go. 
2) Prepare yourself for a bureaucratic nightmare of finding courses and getting them approved as well as trying to figure out what the actual requirements and expectations for each course is. 
3) You need to be able to speak Spanish.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If I had the opportunity to choose my host university again, I would go somewhere else in Spain.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friendships with the locals.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To navigate the system at the university and to engage with the other exchange students. Everything with the university has been a bureaucratic and academic struggle. Additionally, the exchange community is purely based on alcohol and composed of students who seek to party.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
